original.target_description: Study 1, treatment preference ratings; speaker L1 × job prestige × performance level interaction; Calgary listeners rating L1 English versus L1 Tagalog speakers; binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model with logit link.

n.sample_role: analytic rating observations (repeated ratings nested within listeners and speakers)
n.exclusions: Row-wise deletion of missing predictor or response values; initial 576 observations from 96 listeners.
n.quote: In the end, there were 551 observations for the rating of competence, 556 observations for the rating of treatment preference, and 564 observations for the rating of comprehensibility.

es.metric: Estimate (binomial mixed-effects model logit coefficient; standardization not stated)
es.location: p. 19, Table 2, Speaker L1 × Prestige × Skill row

p.location: p. 19, Table 2, Speaker L1 × Prestige × Skill row

replication.target_description: Study 1, treatment preference ratings; speaker L1 × job prestige × performance level interaction; Santa Catarina L1 Brazilian Portuguese listeners rating L1 BP versus L1 Spanish speakers (conceptual replication of the English/Tagalog contrast); binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model with logit link.

n.sample_role: analytic rating observations (repeated ratings nested within listeners and speakers)
n.exclusions: Row-wise deletion of missing values from 360 observations; 60 listeners. Two listeners reporting hearing issues retained because exclusion did not change findings.
n.location: Data analysis, paragraph immediately preceding Results (p. 6)
n.quote: Despite having 360 observations for each response variable, the lme4 function used row-wise deletion to handle missing values. In the end, there were 351 observations for each rating.

es.metric: Estimate (binomial mixed-effects model logit coefficient; standardization not stated)
es.location: p. 9, Table 2, Speaker L1 × prestige × performance row

p.location: p. 9, Table 2, Speaker L1 × prestige × performance row

reported_success.location: Discussion, Competence and treatment preference, p. 14
reported_success.quote: Again, this is opposite to what is reported in Teló et al. (2022), where the sole circumstance favoring treatment by L2 speakers was low-prestige, low-performance scenarios.

notes: Original primary author-hosted PDF title and DOI verified; acquired from https://www.paveltrofimovich.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Telo_et_al_2022.pdf. Replication frozen supplied text matches publisher title/DOI at https://academic.oup.com/applij/article/45/6/1010/7712341. Replication uses BP/Spanish rather than English/Tagalog by design; locator and corresponding conceptual test match. Extracted printed Estimate, not converted to standardized beta. Page numbers refer to author PDF/advance article pagination. Selected the three-way model coefficient, not one of the several low-performance post hoc contrasts; Skill in original tables denotes performance level.
